But then when we come to cut the membrane, which is what it was, you can actually see John putting the scissors into the membrane and the membrane lifting. And as it goes, it's a beautiful effect. Just very, very realistic. (0:56:09)

Yeah, that's right. So yeah, back to the design of the alien. Likewise, with the eyes. I never bought the idea of an alien having these black eyes. Because I know how a lens works. And I don't think that could work. And again, you could say, well, what do you know about aliens? How do you know how aliens work? Well, it's not about that. It's about using your own perception and saying, do I buy this, right? (0:56:40)

So I said to John, what if we make these lenses, right? So it's a modern sunglasses. Okay, because they've got low set, very small ears. They couldn't wear glasses, sunglasses like we do. What if they've evolved and there's just a lens that sits in the eye, and that's why they're all black. And then we can reveal by removing the lens, actually, they've got an eye underneath with an iris and a pupil like we have. (0:57:12)

Yeah, so what we did was we coloured some latex black, and we put some KY jelly into the eyeball that was painted inside. And then we just covered it with KY jelly. And then we painted the black latex on top, let it set. So when we removed it, all the KY jelly is gunky underneath. It's just a great effect. Just a beautiful effect. (0:57:31)

So creative. Yeah, so it's all these little things that sell it. Well, not one thing, there's no one thing. In my book, I'm releasing my book very soon. And in my book, I've got a whole chapter about the backstory about who the alien is, which is what we would be talking about now. That's interesting, because Philip Mantle asked me when your book's coming out, and he also says hi. (0:57:58)

Thank you, Philip. He's going to come on our podcast soon, actually. Oh, good, good. Yeah, a few minutes left. So thank you for all the information. It was very interesting. My pleasure. I mean, my main question really would be, given all that, do you see it as then kind of like, like the purpose of this kind of artistry? Do you see it as about raising awareness of anything, or more just about fun? Or is it like, I think I think that the the UFO community as it's become known, and anyone that believes in aliens and who investigates and studies the subject, they need to be less aggressive towards me, and more grateful. And I'll explain why. (0:58:52)

I showed them that they should question everything. They shouldn't take anything at face value. They should ask questions. And they should ask for evidence. Okay. And my, my film has shown them how easily they can be taken in. Okay. Yeah. So now what they should, what they should do now is they should investigate, ask questions, and demand answers. (0:59:22)

Unfortunately, a lot of them that I found, just jump on a bandwagon, and they believe what they hear. And they actually embellish what they see. And before you know it, it's they saw the alien. Actually, no, no, no. You've got no idea what you're talking about. Because what you've followed, if you follow back of all the things they say, they change their story. (0:59:47)

And this is not rocket science. Okay. I went to Roswell, I spoke to people who are on record as having seen the aliens. Right. And then and then I showed them the film. And this is what they saw. Well, I know they can't be. That means, well, that's interesting. I guess they probably weren't telling, you know, the real truth, so to speak. (1:00:06)

But maybe they thought it was something like, yeah, it's strange. People want to be, people want to belong. I guess what I'm asking is, do you believe there are aliens out there? You know what, you know what, that's a, that's a separate question. Just because my film's not real doesn't mean to say there are no aliens. Right. Okay. I don't know because I've never seen one. (1:00:25)

And I don't, I don't pooh-pooh anybody that says they saw one. But what I do do is I ask questions. Okay. And I, I look at the answers. Now. Okay. So you saw an alien? Yes. Okay. What was it like? What do you mean? What was its demeanour? Was it aggressive? Was it friendly? Was it what was it? Well, I don't know. (1:00:49)

I haven't thought about it. Right. They haven't done the basic groundwork of who is this thing that I'm making up? If you did see it, those people that did see an alien, they have great descriptions and they have great knowledge. Right. So you can decipher very quickly who's telling the truth and who just wants to be special. (1:01:06)

Do you think there was an alien in Roswell? No, personally, I don't believe that was a, that was a UFO crash. I believe it was a military vehicle that crashed. I believe they kept it quiet because it was embarrassing. That's why. Yeah. Yeah. Spiros, please tell me you did the Bigfoot video. No, I didn't. I wish I did. (1:01:34)

I wish I did. I mean, I was going to say, basically, yeah, we're going to conclude in a second, but yeah, thank you for all this. It's been really interesting. I mean, the main thing that I take from all of it is that, yeah, it's very interesting the degree to which people can be led to believe anything. If you, like you say, you present them with the right apparent evidence, even if it's got multiple levels of pretty much what you say, as you've described. (1:01:56)

If you throw in a few truths in anything, right, it's easy to buy it. Okay. So for example, let's talk about, very quickly, let's just talk about the COVID thing again. Okay. If you were to say, right, let's not say COVID, let's say cancer. (1:02:10)

Okay. Let's, I'll just make a blank, I'm going to make a blanket statement. Nobody ever died of cancer. Right? And you can take that information and you can either use it logically, or you can sensationalize it and say, haha, it's a hoax. No one ever died of cancer. Actually, no one ever did die of AIDS. Right? They die of the, of the, of the elements that AIDS creates. (1:02:35)

So for example, yes, right, your body's depleted and something else kills you. Right? Pneumonia, right? Or whatever it might be. So the death certificate says, cause of death, pneumonia, doesn't say, doesn't say HIV, doesn't say AIDS, doesn't say cancer. So what I'm trying to say is a little bit of knowledge. (1:03:01)

Right? I didn't lie to you. It's true. No one ever died of cancer. It's a true statement. But clearly people have died of cancer. Right? But, but technically, I'm correct. Now, if you were a little bit simple, you could carry that and run with it and make it a whole big conspiracy theory about how all these cancer research should, no, no, no, no, no, it's all nonsense. Doesn't exist. No one ever died of cancer. Do you see? (1:03:22)

I think you made a very good point with your alien autopsy video. And especially now in the age where people are so willing to believe stuff that I think it's good. There's people out there who can just push on that. This is the first time you ever saw fake news. Oh, yeah, you created fake news. I'm sorry about that. But this is true. This is true. (1:03:44)

Well, what I'd like to say as well was that like, this is the one thing I was thinking about the way the media does use things. And I think this is why it's very difficult to know what's true and false. Because one thing that can be said is that camera footage, as you've proven, can be falsified. (1:04:03)

Therefore, a lot of things we see on the news and the media can't be taken for granted either. So I think we're in more need than ever now of independent free thinking and honest journalists and filmmakers like yourself and others who want to like small things in a real and informative way. So yeah, thank you very much. Question everything. Absolutely. Thank you very much for attending tonight. (1:04:24)

My pleasure. Superstar. Thank you. I'll send you a copy of... it doesn't go out live. We're going to put some titles on it and stuff and blah, blah, blah. And I'll send you a proof of it before we broadcast. Not a problem. It's been an absolute honour. Thank you so much for... Thank you. My pleasure. Nice to meet you guys. We love you loads. And hopefully get you on again. (1:04:49)

Lovely. Whenever you want. Why not. Indeed. Thank you very much. Take care. Take care. Goodbye. Alright, bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. (1:05:11)

(2025-01-20)

item.title: Katie Paige: 牧場の敷地内で何度も精神が操られた事例
item.content:encoded:
前置き​

Katie Paige（MUFON Colorado 州支部長）のインタビュー動画から。

コメント​

何者かによって「精神を操られた」のではなく、現場の EMF 異常で意識障害が引き起こされたのだろう。現場一帯では、意識障害 ＋ orb によって、怪奇現象が多発しだのだと判断する。

FasterWhisper AI(large-v2 model) + DeepL(2024-07 model)​

そうです。そうです。当時は知らなかった。Dr.スプリンクルズに行って、このファイルを引っ張り出してきて初めて、これらのメモがあったんだ。だから、あの泉にある軍事基地の画像は全部送ったはずだ。エルバート・ランチ そうだ。 (0:22:11)

そうそう。大きな赤い星が牧場のある場所です。この地図には空軍士官学校があります。シャイアン・マウンテンNORAD、フォート・カーソン、シュレディンガー空軍基地、ピーターソン空軍基地。フォート・カーソンのそばには、ヘリコプターがあるビュートもありますね。 (0:22:26)

その昔、70年代後半、空軍士官学校はI-25を挟んで牧場のあるあの辺りに土地を所有していました。 スプリンクルズ博士のファイルには、興味深いメモがありました...ウォーレンと書かれていて、その後フォート・カーソンから再編集されましたが、牧場の敷地内でした。次だ 次はこれです。 (0:22:51)

[OCR]

"Warren xxx, Camp Carson, visits ranch, felt something wrong, wouldn't go into woods, something took over his mind, made him walk toward woods, released him, he could run back - did this 5 times."

「ウォーレン・xxx、キャンプ・カーソン、牧場を訪れ、何か 、おかしいと感じ、森に入ろうとしなかった。何かが彼の心を支配し、森に向かって歩かせ、彼を解放すると、走って戻ることができた。"これを5回繰り返した。

これは...いきますよ。ウォーレン 空白です ウォーレン 空白です レオ・スプリンクルズ博士の 直筆です 牧場を訪問 異変を感じ- 森には入らず 牧場の裏にポンデローサ松の 林があった 何かが彼の心を支配し、森に向かって歩かせ、彼を解放すると逃げ帰ってきたという。そして彼は5回ほど逃げ帰った。 (0:23:12)

DARPAのマインドコントロールのようなものを思い出した。あれはいったい何だったんだろう？ なぜフォート・カーソンの人間が牧場の敷地内にいたのか？私には衝撃的だった。 これはビル・ワーが話していたもので、レオ・スプリンクルズ博士のメモです。保安官のビル・ワウが誰かと話したがっている。 (0:23:36)

[OCR] · "Bill Waugh, undersheriff,wants to talk to someone.

· Has seen ships going into the ground, boxes, mutilations being done.

· Nobody will talk- don't want investigation - publicity.

· No stigma, credentials - important factor.

· John would go back.

· NORAD Col. said bluntly to forget it, shut up.

· Air Force head has a directive to handle UFO's, big bigfoot."

  • "保安官補のビル・ウォーが話したいそうだ。

  • 土に沈む船、箱、切り刻まれるのを見たことがある。

  • 誰も話そうとしない。

  • 汚名がないこと、信用があること、これが重要な要素だ。

  • ジョンは戻るだろう」。

  • NORADの大佐は単刀直入に、忘れろ、黙れ、と言った。

  • 空軍のトップは、UFOやビッグフットを扱えと指令を出している」。

船が地中に沈むのを見た、箱も見た、切断もされた。誰も話そうとしない。 調査も宣伝も望んでいない。汚名を着せたくない。彼にとって資格は重要だった。 それは重要な要素だった。ジョンは戻るだろう。さて、ジョンは私の子供時代から牧場の敷地内にいた大人の一人で、今は他界している。NORADの大佐は、そんなことは忘れろ、黙ってろ、とぶっきらぼうに言ったと書いてあった。 (0:24:05)

動画(52:41)​

Katie Paige - MUFON State Director Colorado

(2025-01-19)

item.title: Katie Paige: 二重反転回転型 UFO の目撃報告
item.content:encoded:
前置き​

珍しい目撃報告。記録に値する。

関連過去記事​

❏ 1970-08, カナダ : 二重反転回転するキノコの傘に似た UFO の詳細　（途中 2） (2024-03-24)

仮説：撮影された UFO の回転対称軸が水平と垂直の二通りである理由 （＋追加） (2024-08-07)

FasterWhisper AI(large-v2 model) + DeepL(2024-07 model)​

本当に興味深い事例です。でも、この話をしたのは、コロラドの牧場での事例で、地元の人たちにインタビューしなければならなかったからです。その中の一人はエルクハンターでした。 彼は昼間にエルバート郡のエリアに出かけていました。そして、興味深いことに、彼は私にこう言いました。この男は何十年もそこに住んでいるそうです。 (0:46:19)

彼は、あそこの森にはとても不気味で決して立ち入らない場所があると言いました。まるで、昼間でもそこには行かないような場所です。でも、彼は私にそのことを話してくれました。彼の名前は明かしませんが、この写真なら共有してもいいと言ってくれました。 （0:46:36）

さて、これは皆さんにも見えるかどうか分かりませんが、ラジオのリスナーのために説明してください。分かりました。ご覧になっているのはこれです。これは本当に信頼できる目撃証言です。彼は消防士です。彼はエルク狩りをしていたところ、2021年11月頃にこのようなことが起こったと言いました。彼は昼間に外に出ていて、木々の間から赤い光、赤とオレンジの光が見えたそうです。 （0:47:02）

そして、彼はその物体の直径は4～5フィートだったと言いました。それは地面から6～8フィート離れていました。そして、彼は、それは2つのバウンドケーキ型が重なり合っているように見えたと言いました。1つは時計回りに、もう1つは反時計回りに回転していました。 彼はその物体をじっと見ていました。まるで音もなく。そして一瞬振り返ると、その物体は消えていました。 （0:47:25）

赤い光はしばらく残っていましたが、その物体は消えました。どこへ行ったのか？離陸するのを見なかったそうです。 （0:47:31）

うん。本当にクールだ。

DS: 本当にクールだ。ちょっとそれを持ったままにしてくれる？ うん、うん。 いいかい。これからとてもとても奇妙なことを話すよ。 それは、僕がこの夏に30ヤード離れた場所から見たものに非常に近いんだ。

KP: まさか。私の見たものは茶色でした。本当ですか？彼はそれをとても金属的で、赤い光沢のあるものだと表現しました。あなたの見たものにも光沢はありましたか？ （0:48:14）

いいえ、マットな茶色でした。太陽の光が反射しているのが見えました。 わあ。そこに生物がいて、木々の間を歩いていました。 そして、私が宇宙船を見た場所に戻ったとき、そこにはもうありませんでした。 離陸するのを見なかったのですか？ 30ヤード離れていました。 （0:48:47）

私たちはそれを聞いたでしょう。私たちは、私たちは、私たちは... どのくらいの数の存在で、彼らはどんな外見でしたか？ 私はその存在を見ていません。他の人たちは見ていました。彼らは灰色で、背の高い灰色でした。

▼原文 展開

It's a really cool case. But I bring it up because in the Colorado ranch case, I've got to interview some locals and one of them is an elk hunter. And he goes out in this Elbert County area in the daytime. And what's fascinating, he'll tell me, this guy's lived there for decades. (0:46:19)

And he's like, there's certain parts of the forest out there where he will not enter because it's just so eerie. Like he, he will not even go there in the daytime, but he shared with me, and I'm not going to give up his name, but he did tell me I could share this picture. (0:46:36)

So this right here, I don't know if you guys could see this, explain it for our radio audience. Okay. So what you're looking at is this, this is a really credible witness. He is a firefighter. And he was out elk hunting and he said this happened approximately November of 2021. He's out there daytime sighting, and he sees a red glow, red, orange glow in the trees. (0:47:02)

And he said this object was four to five feet in diameter. It was six to eight feet off the ground. And he said, it looked like two Bundt cake pans, one on top of the other. One was spinning clockwise. The other was spinning counterclockwise. And he's watching this thing very close. Like he, no sound. And he turns for a second, he looks back and the thing's gone, just disappeared. (0:47:25)

The red glow was there for a little while, but that thing was gone. And where did it go? He didn't see it take off. (0:47:31)

Yeah. So really cool. Really cool. Can you hold that up for a second, please? Yeah. Yes. I want to make sure that we. Okay. That I'm going to tell you something very, very weird. That is extremely close to what I saw this summer, 30 yards away from me. No way. Except mine was brown. Really? And he described this as very metallic, shiny with a red glow. Did yours have a glow to it? (0:48:14)

No, it was like a matte brown color. You could see the sun shining off of it. Wow. And there were beings there and walking through the trees. And when I went back to where I'd seen the craft, it was gone. And you didn't see it take off or... It was 30 yards away. (0:48:47)

We would have heard it. We would have, we would have... How many beings and what did they look like? I didn't see the beings. Other people did. They were gray. They were tall gray.

item.title: 宿命通は（奥義を極めた聖者のみが獲得できる超越的な能力ではなく）意識障害の副産物であることを論証する
item.content:encoded:
前置き​

宿命通とは AI によると…

AI

宿命通（しゅくみょうつう）とは、仏教用語で、前世の自他の生存状態を自在に知ることができる神通力を意味します。六神通（ろくじんずう）のひとつです。﻿

六神通とは、禅定を修めることで得られる超人的な能力のことで、天眼通、天耳通、他心通、宿命通、神足通（神境通）の五神通に漏尽通を加えたものです。﻿

六神通の他の能力には、次のようなものがあります。

  • 天眼通（てんげんつう）：普通の人の見ることのできない事象を自由自在に見通すことのできる力﻿

  • 天耳通（てんにつう）：あらゆる苦悩のうめき声を聞きもらさない耳の力﻿

  • 他心通（たしんつう）：あらゆる苦悩の心のうちを知り尽くす力﻿

  • 神足通（じんそくつう）：思いのままに行きたいところに行けたり、姿を変えることができたり、また環境を変えることのできる力

  • 漏尽（ろじん）通： 煩悩が尽きて、今生を最後に二度と迷いの世界に生まれないことを知る智慧。生まれ変わることはなくなったと知る力

以下では、宿命通について多分これまで誰もなし得なかったであろう説明を試みる。単なる私の憶測ではなく、具体的なデータに基づいて論証を行う。

後日、宿命通を詳しく記述した仏教経典（沙門果経）の該当箇所を引用する予定だが、今は時間がないので OCR 処理まで手が回らない。

粗筋​

最初に、

  1. その具体的なデータを提示し、

  2. 続いてそのデータの意味するところを述べ、

  3. その上で、宿命通が意識障害の副産物であることを論証する。

細かな説明はダルいので、詳しい説明は AI に代わってもらう。

データに関する背景説明​

Anthony Peake が、そのデータを 2つ話題にしてる。最初のデータ（ギロチンの件）は過去記事でも取り上げたが、2番目のデータは初紹介。この 2番目のデータが重要でタイトルの主張に密接に関連する。

データの和訳には「悪魔」となっているが、Anthony Peake が使う Daemon という言葉には彼独特の意味があり、それは短く言えば

ChatGPT-4o

Anthony Peake の「Daemon（デーモン）」は、人間の意識の二重構造を説明する独特な概念です。彼は、日常的で時間に制約された「自己（Eidolon）」と、時間を超越し、過去や未来を見通せる「高次の自己（Daemon）」が存在すると仮定します。「Daemon」は危機的状況で直感や予感を与えるガイド的役割を果たし、Peake の「永遠回帰」仮説では、過去の人生の記憶を持ち、同じ失敗を回避する助けになるとされています。彼はこの仮説を古代哲学、量子物理学、脳科学の観点からも探求し、意識や時間の本質を考える新しい視点を提示しています。

となり、より詳しく言えば

▼ChatGPT-4o 展開

Anthony Peake は、意識や現実の本質を探求する独特な仮説を提唱するイギリスの作家で、特に彼の著作では「Daemon（デーモン）」という概念が中心的な役割を果たしています。この「Daemon」は、伝統的な宗教やオカルトで語られる霊的存在とは異なり、人間の意識や自己の二重性に関する仮説的なモデルとして提案されています。以下に、彼の「Daemon」概念を簡単に解説します。

1. Daemon とは何か？​

Peake の「Daemon」は、古代ギリシャ哲学の「ダイモーン（中間的な霊的存在）」や「高次の自己」に影響を受けています。しかし、彼の解釈ではより心理学的・科学的な側面を持ちます。具体的には、「Daemon」は個人の中に存在する、すべてを知る別の自己または意識の側面を指します。

  • Eidolon（アイドロン）との対比 Peake は、人間の意識を2つの側面に分けて説明します：

    • Eidolon（アイドロン）： 日常的な自己。時間を直線的に体験し、記憶に制約される普通の意識。
    • Daemon（デーモン）： もう1人の自己。時間の制約を超越し、未来や過去の全てを知っている「高次の観察者」的存在。

  • 簡単に言えば、**Eidolon は「今を生きる自分」、Daemon は「全てを見通す内なるガイド」**という構図です。

2. Daemon の役割​

Peake の理論では、「Daemon」は単なる理論上の概念ではなく、私たちの日常生活や体験に直接関係するとされています。

  • 人生の危機におけるガイド Peake は、何らかの危機的状況（例：命の危険、極限状態など）において、「Daemon」が個人に警告や助言を与えることがあると述べています。たとえば、「何かが起こる予感」や「直感的な判断」が「Daemon」による影響だと説明されます。

    催眠状態では意識の通常の抑制機能が低下し、記憶や空想が過剰に活性化することがあります。宿命通の体験も、長期の修行による脳の特異な状態が催眠に似た効果を生み出している可能性があります。

  • 気質・体質による限定性
    宿命通を得られる修行者が極めて少ない点は、これが特定の脳の構造や気質に依存した現象であることを示唆しています。例えば、感受性が高い人や、自己暗示にかかりやすい人ほどこのような体験を得やすいかもしれません。

  • 脳の情報処理の錯誤
    脳は膨大な記憶や情報を保存していますが、その一部を自己のストーリーとして再構築する機能が、修行や瞑想によって異常活性化することで「過去世」をリアルに感じさせる可能性があります。

2. 修行の影響と脳への負荷​

長期にわたる瞑想や修行は、脳の可塑性や認知機能に強い影響を与えることが知られています。この過程で以下のような変化が宿命通に繋がる可能性があります：

  • 自己洗脳の効果
    瞑想の反復により「過去世」という概念を深く内面化することで、脳がそれを現実として「体験」する準備を整える可能性があります。

  • 脳へのダメージや特異な状態
    睡眠不足、極度の集中、栄養不足など、修行の過程で脳が通常とは異なる神経学的状態に陥ることで、非現実的な体験が引き起こされる場合があります。

  • 特定の脳領域の活性化
    瞑想が誘発する特定の脳波（アルファ波、シータ波など）の変化や、海馬や前頭前野など記憶や自己意識に関わる領域の異常活性化が、宿命通体験の一因である可能性があります。

3. 宿命通を「超越」ではなく「錯誤」と見る意義​

  • 神秘性を排除
    宿命通を脳の誤動作や自己暗示と見ることで、超越的な能力としての解釈を排除できます。これは、宿命通を科学的に理解するための第一歩となります。

  • 人間の意識の限界を知る
    宿命通が脳の「錯誤」であるならば、それは意識の持つ創造的側面や脆弱性を理解する上で重要な手がかりとなります。人間の脳がどれだけ「現実」を再構築できるかを示す例と言えるでしょう。

  • 不必要な飛躍を防ぐ
    Peake のように量子論を持ち込むことなく、観察可能な脳の作用や心理学的メカニズムをもとにした説明が可能になります。これは、仮説としての合理性と検証可能性を高めます。

4. さらに深めるべきポイント​

宿命通を脳の現象と見る仮説を補強するために、以下の研究やデータが役立つかもしれません：

  • 瞑想中の脳活動のリアルタイム測定（fMRI、EEG）
  • 催眠中の記憶再構築のプロセスと宿命通の体験比較
  • 宿命通体験者の性格特性や脳の個別差を調べる研究

結論として、宿命通は超越的な能力というよりも、長期の修行による脳の特異な状態が生み出した意識の錯誤現象と捉えるのが合理的です。このように見ることで、宿命通の謎は単なる神秘の領域に留まらず、科学的な探求の対象として扱えるようになるでしょう。

And it's the idea that you know that there's another, almost another version of you that lived a whole life there. (0:28:01)

You know, they've loved, they've had children. And I've had those dreams where I've lived a whole life and you wake up and you have this terrible feeling of loss, you know, that you've lost the people. Now, in that book, I cite many examples from history of this. And one of the examples that I really, really fascinates me was a guy called Alfred Mowry. And Mowry was a psychologist in the 1890s. And when he was a child, he experienced a very, very heavy fever. (0:28:32)

And in the fever, he had a dream and he was involved in the French Revolution. And he was a member of the revolutionary group with Marat and Robespierre and various others. (0:28:41)

And as with the French Revolution, in the dream, he falls foul of Robespierre and he gets a big trial. And in the trial, in the dream, he stands up and he makes a big long speech to defend himself. He's found guilty. He's then taken down and he's taken through the streets of Paris in a tumble up to the Place de la Bastille, where the guillotine was. (0:29:09)

He then stands in front of the guillotine and makes this long speech to the crowds. The crowds cheer and everything else as well. Then he puts his head down to have his head chopped off and something hit him on the back of the neck. And it was the bed board. The bed board had come loose and it had fallen down and hit him on the back of the head. (0:29:28)

Now that intrigued me and it intrigued him for one important reason. A whole dream had been back created to accommodate what happened at the end of the dream. Now think about that for a second. This is extraordinary. His dream went back in time in order to create a whole story to have him being hit by a guillotine. That's why he became a psychologist because he was interested in this time dilation thing. (0:29:55)

The second example is even more extraordinary. There was a hypnotist. I can never quite remember his name. It will come to me in a second. And he hypnotised a young student. And he hypnotised the student and said, right, I hypnotise you and you're going back. And the student found himself in a dream sequence, standing in a field with long grass. (0:30:24)

And he feels hungry. And he walks through the long grass and he hears a child crying. He looks down and he sees a baby lying in a swaddling thing. And he realises the baby's hungry. And he realises the baby's hungry because he's the baby. And then the baby's parents turn up and they pick the baby up and they feed him and they put him in the pram and they take him away. (0:30:52)

The student followed that child right through his life until he was 16. Minute by minute, he lived this kid's whole life and experienced things and guided this kid. He was a daemon, effectively. Then when the kid decides to go to university, suddenly he finds himself waking up and he's in the room. He'd been away for about half an hour in a trance. He'd lived 16 years in a trance situation, witnessing somebody else's life. (0:31:18)

Now, again, if you don't believe me about that story, I give the references in the book. And I'll try and remember the name of the author, but it is in a book written by Aldous Huxley. A lot of people believe that that story was Aldous Huxley himself, but it wasn't. The dates don't mix. And in my new book, I say that the dates don't mix in terms of that. (0:31:38)

But suffice to say, it means that in dream sequences, we're in different worlds, we're in different perceptual fields. And I think your example is a classic there. (0:31:50)

You know, that's... do you lucid dream? Have you lucid dreamed? I've had maybe, yeah, I've had like two or three lucid dreams I can remember in the last five years. I had one where I was actually in the toilet. And I was like in a... I guess I was like in a prison or jail, maybe because I was watching too many prison shows. (0:32:15)

And I was... there were like, you know, like the convicts or a few convicts, and they were just like right there. And I'm like, man, I'm looking and I'm like, I have no privacy. And I'm just like, this has got to be a dream. And one of them said, this ain't no dream, man. And I remember thinking, oh, my God, I can't believe it's real. (0:32:38)

And then when I woke up, and I remember, I remember the dream precisely. And I'm thinking, man, that was so real. Like, I really felt like that was real. So maybe that's not a lucid dream. But it was one of those dreams where you're questioning whether it's real or not in the dream. And then I came to the conclusion in the dream that I thought it was real. (0:33:01)

I think that's the point. It's the point where you become self-aware of the fact of who you are in a dream. As people like Robert Wagoner argues, you know, one of the major researchers in lucid dreaming, you know, we're incredibly stupid when we're in lucid dream states. You know, we see the most ridiculous things, and we never think I'm in a dream. (0:33:20)

And this is what happened to me. My lucid dream was quite strange. By the way, the person, I've remembered the person's name, because I've just written it down while you were talking. It was a guy called Erickson. Okay. That did the stuff. But I was in a nightclub. I used to be a clubber when I was younger, and I found myself in a nightclub. (0:33:34)

This was about 18 months ago, two years ago. And in the dream, I'm in a nightclub, and I come outside the nightclub, and I'm walking down an alleyway. And I think to myself, why am I in a nightclub? And then I felt the duvet around me. And I thought, you're not in a nightclub, you're dreaming. And then for the first time, and the only time in my life, I became aware in the dream. (0:33:56)

And I'm standing there looking down at my hands, and I'm going, what do I do now? And I thought, in dreams, what you can do is you can fly. So I decided to see, I thought, can I fly? So I lifted my legs up, and I fell to the floor, and I actually felt my knees hit the ground. And then I tried it again, and I found myself rising. (0:34:17)

And it was extraordinary. And the thing is with lucid dreams, they're in your mind forever. I can still see this. And then I fly up, and there was a back wall to the alleyway, and I flew over the back wall to see a bay. (0:34:28)

It was a seaside resort, and there were cars and lights. It was late at night, and there were cars and lights driving along. It was real. I could feel the wind around me, and I'm flying, and I'm going, this is absolutely extraordinary. And then I woke up. But that was, I think, the most amazing experience I think I've had, because it made me realise that this reality is no more a dream than that reality. (0:34:57)

And lucid dreaming friends of mine, and I can put you in contact with a number of lucid dreamers that do a lot of work on this. They go back to the same place. They are drawing maps of their world. There's a friend of mine at the moment, Samantha, and she is doing work. She dreams about a place called future Tokyo. And she's walking around in this place, in future Tokyo. And she's met people in future Tokyo that she's met in real life, who recognised her from the dream sequence. (0:35:36)

So what is happening here? So are there levels of consciousness that we can flick within? So it's not just the Bohmian IMAX. It's far more, it's like mirrors. Because, for instance, there's something called false awakenings. And I don't know if you've ever done this. It's happened to me a few times, but the best I've ever heard was somebody that happened eight times. (0:35:59)

So what you're doing is you're lying in bed, and you wake up. And you get up, you go to the bathroom, you clean your teeth, and you wake up again. And you go to the bathroom, you clean your teeth, you go downstairs, and you start having breakfast, and you wake up again. This happened to this guy eight times. (0:36:11)

He got to the middle of the afternoon, and he was in work. And he's with his workmates. And he looks out through the window, and it was a summer's afternoon, and it was dark outside the windows. And he thought, why is it dark outside? And he woke up again. (0:36:27)

And as he said to me, in the message to me, he said, how do I know that that last waking up was into not another dream? And that's so true. Because how do we know we are not dreaming now? What can tell us that we're not dreaming? There's nothing. So is life a dream? And at the end of the dream, you just wake up again, and live your life again. You know, so then it comes back again to cheating the ferryman. (0:36:51)

And the whole idea that everything is perceptual, everything is information, everything is being perceived. Yeah, well, Henry David Thoreau said, you know, in our dreams, you know, basically, it's our truest life. Our truest life is when we are in our dreams awake. That was a quote by Henry David Thoreau. And actually, that's the basis for my next video. (0:37:21)

And I'm talking about that. So it's interesting you're bringing this all up. Can I make one more of the point? (0:37:24)

Sure. Sure, please. This might be interested in this as well, is that I wrote a book on out-of-body experiences. And I have a model I call the intrasomatic and extrasomatic models, whereby I believe that we exist within when we're in out-of-body states, it's kind of brain created, but not. It's again, this kind of a Gregorial model. But I was reminded of something that a number of friends of mine have said take place with them when they are in dream states, when they're in lucid dream states, they're in the body of somebody else. (0:37:59)

Again, Samantha has told me she's in the body of somebody that's not her. And she sometimes catches the reflection of this person in mirrors, and it's not her, it's somebody else. And some of you may be aware of the writings of Robert Monroe, the out-of-the-body guy. And I... That was Tom Campbell's... Tom Campbell worked with him, correct. (0:38:22)

And Monroe, in one of his books, has a concept called either. And when he was in out-of-body states, he would suddenly find himself inside somebody else's body. And there was one classic example of this where Monroe is sleeping and wakes up inside the body of either. Now this either person existed in a totally different world, the cars were slightly different, and the fashions were slightly different. (0:38:45)

And indeed, I'll send you a link that you need to put up on this, is an associate of mine has done a short film based upon the concept of either, based on a village in Croatia, which is really interesting to watch. I'll send you the link. But either, what happened? He found himself in the body of either. (0:39:09)

And he's sitting in his living room, and there's two businessmen sitting opposite him. And behind the businessman is either's wife. Okay. And he realises he's in a business meeting, and he's about to pitch for a business deal. But he doesn't know what the business deal is for. So he starts waffling. Because he's in either's body. And he said he saw his wife in either looking at him going, what's wrong with you? And then he found himself back in bed being himself again. (0:39:38)

Now, if this is a fact, this is intriguing. Because this can explain petty malabsences that people have when they have temporal lobe epilepsy. It can explain almost possession. You know, when people say people are possessed. You know, there's a term in parapsychology, a term called drop-ins. And these are circumstances whereby a medium will be talking, and a spirit will be talking through the medium. (0:40:04)

And then suddenly something else comes in that's completely different. And one classic example of this was a guy called Ingrida Ingridisson, who in about 1904-1905 was a very famous Icelandic medium. And he's doing his normal medium session on a Friday night, I think it was, something like that. And he's talking in voices. And then suddenly this other voice comes in and turns around and says, you need to know this. And everybody's shocked and said, what? (0:40:31)

The voice says, there's a fire. The fire is happening at the moment. And the person asks, and one of the people asked, where? He said, in Copenhagen. In Konigstrasser. In Copenhagen, there is a fire. 15 Konigstrasser. It's on fire. There's fire engines there. It's burning down. (0:40:49)

And then the voice turns around and says, I've got to go now. I'll come back in 20 minutes and give you an update. And the medium then starts talking in his normal way, comes to him and said, did you know what just happened? And the medium said no. They said, well, let's wait a few hours and see what happens. (0:41:06)

A few hours later, he's sitting and suddenly this voice comes back in again. And it says, yeah, the fire brigade have sorted it out now. It's all right now. It's sorted out. Okay. Now, Iceland at that time was part of Denmark. But the only communications, the newspapers only came through on the ships that came through. There was no other form of communication. So they had to wait for two or three days for the newspapers to come through from Copenhagen to discover that there had been a fire in Königstrasser, number 15 Königstrasser. And the fire had taken place exactly as described by the drop-in, exactly as described. (0:41:40)

Now, subsequently, Professor Erlendur Haraldsson, who was a professor who died recently, professor of psychology at the University of Iceland, took himself over to check up on this case. And the drop-in gave a name. I can't remember the name he called himself. But Haraldsson checked up. This was only about four or five years ago. Haraldsson checked up on this. And lo and befold, not only did he find that the man whose name in question existed, but he lived in a flat at number 17, I think it was, Königstrasser, which was exactly the viewpoint that the drop-in was explaining he was seeing. (0:42:27)

Now, that is extraordinary, because that means a living person had communicated with a medium who was, what, 700-800 miles away, and had precisely given information. And not only that, but had gone away and come back again and given information. Now, that to me is one of the most extraordinary cases. It doesn't mean it was a spirit, doesn't mean it was a dead person. (0:42:54)

It was a live person communicating with somebody else. A classic case of telepathy, in my opinion. And I cite that in one of my books. Well, I love when you tell stories like that. It's fascinating. You have a certain way of telling it that really grips the viewer. So I appreciate that. I know we're coming up on towards the end of the time. (0:43:16)

I don't want to take your whole day, but I just had a couple of questions. One is, what is your whole take on the Mandela Effect? Do you think it's real? Is it a psyop? Have you studied it? I mean, how would it play into your theory? Because it's something, I don't know, that I find interesting. I've made a few videos on it. (0:43:30)

So do I. I find it intriguing, because initially, my initial reaction is, I'm quite a skeptic about most things. I don't tend to believe things. And I thought, no, come on, it's bad memory. It's people who are just confusing their memories, you know, until a guy called Jim... Jim Etherett. Oh, God, my brain's gone again. (0:43:56)

But who did one of my interviews that I interviewed recently. And he was saying to me, he said, well, have you heard of the case of Dolly? And I said, no. And he said, do you know the famous James Bond movie where you have jaws? And I said, yes. And he said, do you know the film? And I said, only vaguely. (0:44:16)

He said, do you remember the ending? And I said, yeah, vaguely. And he said, do you remember there's the young girl and jaws goes over to her? And I said, yeah. And I said, she smiles and she's got braces on her teeth like jaws, and they fall in love and they kiss because they've got that link. And he said, do you know that never happened? And I said, nonsense. (0:44:39)

And he said, no, look at the film. And I checked it and it didn't. And everybody I know who knows that movie remembers that scene and it never happened. And it doesn't make sense because that's what brought them together is they both had... Yeah. And I can't, and it completely changed my opinion because, you know, although, you know, my opinion can be changed, you know, by the facts, you know, if it's facts, I'll change my opinion. And I thought, well, is there something more to this? (0:45:10)

And could it be that sometimes we flick within the instantation, within the simulation, and the past changes in some way? And I know of all the other examples, and the other examples are all interesting. You know, like the Coca-Cola sign. I mean, I'm sure that there was a little thing at the bottom. (0:45:38)

And I'm also sure that I remember the guy in Monopoly having a monocle, you know, and I can't prove that, but I just find it. Is it just that we have expectations of things and we then remember the expectations rather than the actuality? And I don't know, but the Mandela effect does intrigue me. I have to say it's something that is one of the few things that I think, hmm, strange. (0:46:04)

Do I believe that the Large Hadron Collider caused it? No, I don't. But it is still strange and peculiar. Right. To me, it just proves or shows that this whole reality is a lot more malleable than people think. Yes. I think that collectively, as I argue in my book, and I'll be working on this in the future, this idea of, as I said, the egregorial reality, is that if we anticipate, if we collectively believe in things, they happen. (0:46:31)

I'll give an example of this. In my last book, I discuss about the Marian apparitions in Fatima in 1917 in Portugal. And there was something happened there extremely strange, where the sun danced in the sky and it came down towards Earth. Now, my mother was a Roman Catholic and she used to cite this case. (0:46:58)

And as a kid, you know, I'm not religious, and I used to turn around and say, oh, for crying out loud, the sun, if I know enough about astronomy, if the sun span in the sky, it just doesn't do that. The Earth would have to have been moving, not the sun. And I dismissed it. (0:47:14)

But I started researching it. And there were about 7000 people witnessed this event. And not only that, but the actual, there were scientists there who witnessed it. (0:47:18)

And it had been raining beforehand, and the rain evaporated. Now, the only thing I can think of was it was a collective hallucination. But that doesn't explain the rain evaporating. You know, you can say that lots of people saw it. And of course, scientists do this all the time, don't they? They have this terminology that they use, that if I see something weird, it's an hallucination, and it's dismissed. (0:47:46)

If you and I see something strange, it's what's called a foliateur, whereby we are collectively influencing ourselves into seeing something that's not there. My counter argument to that was, well, that suggests telepathy, which science also doesn't accept. But they use one thing they don't believe in to dismiss something else they don't believe in even more. (0:48:05)

Okay, so then we get that. And then you get collective hallucinations where thousands of people see things. But our modern science can't explain that. They can't explain it. It's a label. They love giving things labels, better with a nice Latin name or a Greek name, because that gives it... it's like, I don't know, idiomatic epilepsy. (0:48:29)

So somebody will... the doctor will turn around and say, you have idiomatic epilepsy, and sit back as if he's actually solved it. Then you go to the dictionary and check the word idiomatic. And it means from unknown source. In other words, you have epilepsy, and I haven't got a bloody clue what's causing it. And that is how science works. (0:48:50)

They give things labels to confuse us and make us think that they know what they're bloody well talking about, when the fact of the matter is, for most of the time, they don't. You know, they know some things. Going back to my point earlier, that every science believes that it has the answers. (0:49:08)

We will find a new paradigm is on the door. It's going to be dawning soon, where we will make some discoveries scientifically, which will throw out the present paradigm, just as Copernicus and Kepler threw away the Aristotelian worldview of the universe, and the Earth is the centre of the universe. It's going to happen again. And it will happen many times. (0:49:31)

We shouldn't sit back and think that we are the pinnacle of scientific expertise, until we can explain things such as dark matter, until we can explain how 94% of the universe is missing, until we can bring together the maths of quantum physics and cosmology and relativity, until we can explain the placebo effect and the nocebo effect. We don't know. Yeah, I believe there's Will Durant who said, every science begins as philosophy and ends as art. (0:49:57)

But I was gonna say, so we're coming up on time here. We have Zoom set for two hours. So I don't know what happens after two hours. But I wanted, you know, before that happens, can you tell people, you know, the best place to find you? I know you all your books are on Amazon. But if you and if you wanted to talk about a little bit more about your next book, when it's going to come out and, you know, a little bit, well, basically anything you want to mention? (0:50:27)

Absolutely. Okay. If you want to contact me, the best place normally is Facebook. I'm extremely active on Facebook. Just look up Anthony Peake, you'll find me. At the moment, I'm always at my 5000 limits of Facebook friends, but you can still follow. And I've got about 6000 followers that are on there as well. (0:50:47)

So there's about 11,000 people involved in our community at the moment. And it's growing all the time. So join me on there. Also, I now have a comparatively new YouTube channel, which is proving very popular. I have something called the Anthony Peake Consciousness Hour, which goes out once a month, where I have quite top guests. (0:51:09)

Also, I have Incon, which goes out live on Facebook every Monday afternoon at three o'clock, where I have guests. And you can just watch that. That's then recorded and uploaded onto my channel as well. In terms of my website, it's anthonypeake.com. Again, you can get my books in bookshops. You can go and order a bookshop. (0:51:28)

Many bookshops stock my books. Libraries, you'll find the books. I was delighted to discover that the New York City Library has all of my books there as well. So you can find my books in most libraries. If they're not in the library, you can order them. I don't care. I don't mind. I want people to read the books. (0:51:45)

I'm not after the income. I'm after the book, after people getting the ideas across. My books are also available on Kindle, on eBooks generally. Four of my books are now out on Audible, three of whom are me reading them. And one of them is of an actor reading one of the books. (0:52:06)

They're proving extremely popular and people really like that. They seem to like listening to me droning on about my ideas and reading them. So you can check them out on those. Also, you can download a sample of all of those as well on Amazon, if you wish that. What else can I tell you? Yeah, the books, if you want signed copies of my books, they're available off my website, but it's not important because I'm finding these days the cost of sending the books over because it's just the cost. So when is your new book coming out? (0:52:34)

Yep, the new book will be out probably in March of this year. And what it is, is an updating of my first book is The Life After Death, and it's going to be called Cheating the Ferryman. And it will be a complete update of everything I've been discussing today, with all the new science, with all the stuff I've discovered and read about since 2006, when the first book came out. (0:53:00)

I'm delighted with this book. I think it's going to be, it's going to fascinate a lot of people. There's an awful lot of very, very powerful information in there. Again, it starts with the science and takes you through. So I'm delighted about that. Also, my latest book, The Hidden Universe, is also well worth a read. I'm very, very proud of that book. (0:53:24)

Also, just check me out on YouTube. There's tons of material on YouTube. Google me, it's all there. I know you said that your experience is always updating, you're always learning. And so your books show that. But if somebody had never read you before, never read one of your books, would you suggest that they start at the very beginning, your first book? That is the book that has proved the most popular over the years. (0:53:51)

And I think probably the first, but what I would suggest is, if you want to really understand my work, probably read the first book is The Life After Death, and then read The Hidden Universe, which is my latest book, and then get hold of the new book when it comes out. Because I think that really defines what I'm about and what I'm trying to do. (0:54:13)

All I'd stress is, you know, that I'm a searcher like you. I have no special skills, no special anything. I'm just an ordinary guy pursuing his interests. And fortunately, you know, over 100,000 people worldwide, more than 100,000 people have bought my books over the years. And I thank them for that because without the readers, I'm nobody. And without the information that's sent through to me, I'm nobody. (0:54:35)

I want the feedback. We are an international community. You know, it's not me. People are now taking my ideas and writing books on them and everything else as well. It's going forward. (0:54:45)

You know, it's not looking back and it's not the Anthony Peake show. It's far bigger than that. It's the start of something really quite extraordinary and quite special. So please join in. I will try and respond to emails. I try to, but at the moment, I'm inundated. You know, I'm getting 50 or 60 messages a day on Facebook, plus probably 30 or 40 emails. (0:55:10)

And I'm finding it very difficult to keep up with it. But I will try. Please don't think that I'm ignoring your messages. I'm not. It's just I don't earn a great deal for my writing. So therefore I don't have secretaries and people to do it. It's just me. Well, you say you're not special, but I'm sure I speak for others who know of your work that you are. (0:55:31)

You are Anthony. You know, you're a unique individual and you bring something to the world that nobody else can do. So thank you for that. Thank you so much for your time. Thank you, Chad. It's wonderful. Thanks. Thanks again for giving me the opportunity to talk to you. Bye-bye. Bye-bye. Wow, guys, that was quite an interview. (0:55:48)

I think one of the best ever on my channel. And again, if you haven't watched part one, you can watch it right here. Anthony never ceases to amaze me with the things that he says. I hope you guys enjoyed it. And I hope that everybody kind of understood what Anthony's saying. He's saying basically that we live this perpetual Groundhog's Day again and again. (0:56:06)

And I'm curious to know, do you believe more in what Anthony says or do you more in what I talk about and Tom Campbell, in which we live different lives over and over? I'm curious to know. Let me know in the comments section. And guys, please remember to subscribe and click that notification bell. (0:56:21)

So you're alerted to my future content because I wouldn't want to miss you. And if you've noticed, I've been pumping out the content regularly the last few days. This is the third video in three days. And I have another one coming out tomorrow, not an interview, but a regular video. And I think you're really going to enjoy it. And that is because of the people supporting me on Patreon and PayPal. And this enables me to put out that content regularly. So big thank you. If you want to support the channel, links are below. (0:56:44)

And I just want to say another big thank you to everybody who watched this video all the way until the end. I love you guys. And I'll see you all in the next video. Much peace and love. Namaste. (0:56:54)

(2025-01-18)

item.title: 存在の本質：「身体（ロボット）を備えた AI」によって「自己の実存」と「世界の成立」が同時に発生する
item.content:encoded:
前置き​

意味不明なタイトルだが、忘れないうちに雑メモとして記録する。

説明がダルいので AI との対話で代替えする。今の AI はまだ洞察が乏しく、凡庸な見解も目に付くので、そういった箇所は折りたたんでおく。

後日、書式を整えたいところ。タイトルも工夫すべきだが。

対話​

Me:

文脈は AI ＋ロボットです。現状、最先端の AI といえど、（ロボットの）身体をもちません。いずれ、身体を持つAI が登場した時、AI それ自身の意識にどのような変化が期待できますか？

ChatGPT
Details

▼展開 AIが身体を持つようになった場合、その「意識」に関連してどのような変化が期待できるかについては、以下の観点から考察できます。
